content.description: Illustration showing correct and wrong method of removing high-tension cords by rubber boots

items: CAREFULLY REMOVE HIGH TENSION CORDS BY RUBBER THEIR BOOTS

INSPECT CORD TERMINALS
Check the terminals for corrosion, breaks or distortion.
Replace wire as required.

CHECK WIRE RESISTANCE
Using an ohmmeter, check that the resistance does not exceed the maximum. Replact the cord as required.
Maximum resistance:  25 kΩ per cord

content.text:
DO NOT pull on the wires.
The conductor inside may be damaged.

content.text:
• NEVER USE WIRE BRUSH FOR CLEANING
• NEVER ATTEMPT TO ADJUST GAP ON USED PLUG
• SPARK PLUGS SHOULD BE REPLACED EVERY 60,000 miles (100,000 km)

content.description: Illustration showing megger test setup with spark plug, measuring insulation resistance between electrode and ground

items:
INSPECT ELECTRODE
(a)  If using a megger (insulation resistance meter):
     Measure the insulation resistance.

     Correct insulation resistance:  More than 10 MΩ
     If less than 10 MΩ, clean the plug. (See page IG-6)

content.text:
(b)  If not using a megger:
     Quickly race the engine to 4,000 rpm five times.
     Visually inspect the spark plugs.

     If the electrode is dry ..... Okay
     If the electrode is wet ..... Replace the plug
